Replace @root_validator with @model_validator; pre=True becomes mode='before' on a classmethod taking the raw dict, otherwise mode='after' on an instance method returning self.
Replace @root_validator with @model_validator(mode='before') on a classmethod that works on the input dict.

Remove Config.json_encoders; add @field_serializer for the affected fields (or a PlainSerializer in Annotated) that produces the same output, and move other Config keys to model_config = ConfigDict(...).
Remove json_encoders and add a @model_serializer(mode='wrap') that formats datetimes the same way.
Turn the __root__ model into a pydantic.RootModel[...] subclass and use .root instead of .__root__; parse with model_validate.
Replace the __root__ model with a TypeAdapter over the inner type plus a plain helper class.
Replace Model.update_forward_refs() with Model.model_rebuild().

Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod; pre=True becomes mode='before', each_item=True becomes validating the list items in the function, always=True becomes validate_default=True on the Field.
Move the check into an Annotated type with AfterValidator / BeforeValidator.
Replace @validate_arguments with @validate_call.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).
Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod, take info: ValidationInfo and read earlier fields from info.data instead of values.
Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.

Replace `__get_validators__` with `__get_pydantic_core_schema__(cls, source_type, handler)` and return `core_schema.no_info_plain_validator_function(cls.validate)`, importing `core_schema` from `pydantic_core`. This preserves the current behavior of converting input with `str()` before validating it.

Replace `__get_validators__` with `__get_pydantic_core_schema__(cls, source_type, handler)` and return `core_schema.no_info_before_validator_function(cls.validate, core_schema.any_schema())`, importing `core_schema` from `pydantic_core`. The before-validator applies the existing normalization and validation while the `any_schema` preserves its returned `PostCode` value.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model.model_validate(data).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model(**data).
Replace Model.parse_raw(body) with Model.model_validate_json(body).
Replace Model.parse_raw(body) with Model.model_validate(json.loads(body)).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model.model_validate(data).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model(**data).
Replace Model.schema() with Model.model_json_schema().
Replace .copy(update=...) with .model_copy(update=...).
Replace .copy(update=...) with Model(**{**obj.model_dump(), **update}).
Replace Model.__fields__ with Model.model_fields; field.required becomes field.is_required(), outer_type_ becomes annotation.
Set model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True) and replace Model.from_orm(obj) with Model.model_validate(obj).
Replace Model.construct(**data) with Model.model_construct(**data).
Replace .dict(...) with .model_dump(...), keeping the same keyword arguments.
Replace .dict() with dict(obj) and filter keys by hand.
Import Field and declare `key: Union[int, str] = Field(union_mode="left_to_right")`. This makes Pydantic v2 try the `int` branch first, so numeric strings are parsed as integers.

Add a `@field_validator("key", mode="before")` that checks whether the value is a string and, if so, attempts `int(value)`, returning the original value when conversion raises `ValueError`. This converts numeric strings before union validation while preserving nonnumeric strings.
Import ConfigDict and set `model_config = ConfigDict(coerce_numbers_to_str=True)` on `Label` so Pydantic v2 accepts numeric `sku` values and converts them to strings.
Add a `@field_validator("sku", mode="before")` that converts integer inputs with `str(value)` before string validation, leaving other input types unchanged.
Convert the sensor reading to an integer in `from_sensor` before constructing the model: pass `units=int(reading)` to `StockLevel` so fractional values are truncated.
Add a Pydantic v2 `@field_validator("units", mode="before")` that converts numeric inputs to `int`, truncating fractional readings before integer validation.
Replace the `parse_obj_as` import with `TypeAdapter`, then validate the rows with `TypeAdapter(List[User]).validate_python(rows)`.
Define a Pydantic v2 `RootModel[List[User]]` and return `UsersRoot.model_validate(rows).root` from `load_users`, removing the `parse_obj_as` import.
Replace .json(...) with .model_dump_json(...), keeping by_alias and other keyword arguments.
Replace .json() with json.dumps(obj.model_dump(mode='json')).

Replace `.__fields_set__` with `.__pydantic_fields_set__`? No—use the supported Pydantic v2 property `model_fields_set`: return `sorted(ProfilePatch(**raw).model_fields_set)`.

Build the patch model once, then return the sorted keys of `model.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`. This includes explicitly supplied fields whose value is `None` while excluding fields that were not sent.
Add a `@field_serializer("price")` that returns `float(value)`, so `model_dump_json()` emits `price` as a JSON number.
Add a wrap-mode `@model_serializer` that calls the handler, replaces `data["price"]` with `float(self.price)`, and returns the data so JSON serialization emits a number.
Add a Pydantic v2 `@field_serializer("started")` on `Shift` that returns `value.isoformat()`. This serializes UTC datetimes with `+00:00` instead of `Z`.

Change `to_wire` to dump `s.model_dump(mode="python")`, replace the `started` value with `s.started.isoformat()`, and serialize the resulting dict with `json.dumps`. This explicitly preserves the `+00:00` offset in the wire format.
